narrative:
The model determined that you have a 54% chance of representing a bad credit risk. Because this probability exceeds the threshold the bank uses for approval, your loan application was denied.

The three factors that most strongly influenced this outcome were your credit history, the status of your checking account, and the type of property you own. Your credit history had the largest impact and pushed the decision toward denial. Having no credits or all paid is very uncommon among approved applicants (only 1% of them share this profile), whereas most successful applicants have an existing paid credit history. This absence of a proven track record of managing credit weighed heavily against your application.

The status of your checking account was the second most important factor and also increased the likelihood of being seen as higher risk. Your balance falls in the 0-200 DM range, which is less favorable than the none or higher-balance accounts more commonly seen among approved borrowers.

Your ownership of real estate worked in your favor and was the only major factor pulling the prediction toward approval. However, this positive element was not strong enough to overcome the concerns raised by your credit history and checking account status.

To improve your chances on future applications, focus on building a consistent credit history through timely repayments on smaller obligations, and consider maintaining a healthier checking account balance. These steps will directly address the main reasons your application was declined. (248 words)
